name: Controllers
description: You are at your grandparents' house and you are playing an old video game on a strange console. Your controller has only two buttons and each button has a number written on it. Initially, your score is $$$0$$$. The game is composed of $$$n$$$ rounds. For each $$$1\le i\le n$$$, the $$$i$$$-th round works as follows. On the screen, a symbol $$$s_i$$$ appears, which is either $$$\texttt{+}$$$ ( plus ) or $$$\texttt{-}$$$ ( minus ). Then you must press one of the two buttons on the controller once . Suppose you press a button with the number $$$x$$$ written on it: your score will increase by $$$x$$$ if the symbol was $$$\texttt{+}$$$ and will decrease by $$$x$$$ if the symbol was $$$\texttt{-}$$$. After you press the button, the round ends. After you have played all $$$n$$$ rounds, you win if your score is $$$0$$$. Over the years, your grandparents bought many different controllers, so you have $$$q$$$ of them. The two buttons on the $$$j$$$-th controller have the numbers $$$a_j$$$ and $$$b_j$$$ written on them. For each controller, you must compute whether you can win the game playing with that controller.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2\cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of rounds. The second line contains a string $$$s$$$ of length $$$n$$$ — where $$$s_i$$$ is the symbol that will appear on the screen in the $$$i$$$-th round. It is guaranteed that $$$s$$$ contains only the characters $$$\texttt{+}$$$ and $$$\texttt{-}$$$. The third line contains an integer $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le q \le 10^5$$$) — the number of controllers. The following $$$q$$$ lines contain two integers $$$a_j$$$ and $$$b_j$$$ each ($$$1 \le a_j, b_j \le 10^9$$$) — the numbers on the buttons of controller $$$j$$$.
output_specification: Output $$$q$$$ lines. On line $$$j$$$ print $$$\texttt{YES}$$$ if the game is winnable using controller $$$j$$$, otherwise print $$$\texttt{NO}$$$.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1776L — Controllers [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
